newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian cargo managers back surcharge conduct code.
newsitem.headline: Belgian cargo managers back surcharge conduct code.

text.p: The Belgian airline cargo managers association (ACMAB) said it would back a code of conduct for air cargo surcharges, including those resulting from rise in fuel costs.

Major European airlines from Britain, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Switzerland and Italy have recently introduced, or plan to introduce, a cargo fuel surcharge averaging US10 cents a kg to worldwide destinations, with some exceptions on shorter routes.

ACMAB president, Marcel Buelens, said, "Essentially the airline managers in Brussels are following orders from their head offices. The fuel surcharges had to be implemented. We regret it but we have to keep the aircraft flying."
There should be a formula covering all the factors involved including aircraft fuel prices, he added. This should be agreed by the airlines, shippers and forwarders, he said.

"If there was an index there would be no surprises." Industry sources say Belgian shippers -- manufacturers and exporters -- have advocated a ban of carriers introducing the fuel surcharges and also suggested more use of integrators, such as Federal Express Corp.
Buelens added: "We, the carriers, are partners with the shippers and I am not happy myself with the way the surcharges have been added."
"The industry has not been professional enough," he said.
However, commenting on the recent surcharges he added, "In the last five months we have seen a 20 to 30 percent increase in fuel costs, it was a question of survival."

The 254 member International Air Transport Association (IATA) will hold an emergency meeting in Geneva on November 13 to review the impact of rising fuel costs. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
